sardar-sarovar.whole: The dam promised water to 1.8 million hectares. India's national auditor put command-area development at 341,000 hectares by March 2009, about 19% of that (Governance Now). In 2019 a farmers' group, citing the dam's last annual report, said about 673,000 hectares were actually irrigated, against a Gujarat government claim of 1.49 million made irrigable, with 8,872 km of canals still pending.

CAO appraisal gives no jobs, smallholder or output figures. tata-mundra.whole: The 4,000 MW plant sells power to five Indian states; Tata Power reported 62,946 million units generated from 2012 to 2015, about 2% of India's needs. Business Today reported in 2020 that, after winning on the lowest tariff and then being hit by an Indonesian ban on below-market coal exports, it had made a profit only once in eight years, lost about Rs 11,000 crore and shut most units for a time. No independent evaluation of its effect on supply or prices was found.
tata-mundra.searched: Energetica India reporting Tata Power; Business Today; GEM wiki. No IFC evaluation or independent supply study opened.

grasberg-freeport.whole: The insurance covered a copper and gold mine. An undated Northern Miner report, largely Freeport's account, says it paid Indonesia's central government $1.25 billion in taxes, royalties and dividends since 1992 and had 14,000 direct and contract staff at the end of 1998, about 20% from Papua. No independent audit of those figures, or measure of benefit to Amungme people, was found.

agua-zarca-berta-caceres.whole: The dam, 21.3 MW by its lender FMO's count, was to supply power where, FMO says, 45% of rural households have none, and to raise local living standards and employment. FMO says communities welcomed jobs and income from it, without figures, and that it completed its exit in July 2017 after the project stalled. No source found shows power generated or counts jobs delivered.

No measured output or independent evaluation of who received the power was found.

olkaria-maasai.whole: The project added geothermal power, which the Inspection Panel says reduces Kenya's dependency on fossil fuels. Kenyan press reported that the 280 MW would save about Sh25 billion ($270 million) a year, and the chief executive of the operator KenGen said the fuel charge fell 65% from August 2014 to February 2015. No independent check of the savings, or of how much of that fall came from this plant, was found.

cambodia-microfinance-land-loss.whole: A German government-funded University of Duisburg-Essen survey of Cambodia's microfinance sector, not IFC's clients alone, found 55.5% of 1,388 random households held microloans averaging $5,183 (The Diplomat, 2022). Much debt served investment and "the majority achieves its purpose", while many loans covered living costs, just under half of borrowers had repayment trouble and 6.2% of 964 recent borrowers sold land to repay. No benefit measure for IFC's clients was found.

The regulator NEPRA records 363.71 GWh in June 2025, 70.85% of dependable capacity; no yearly total was opened. AidData's record says it reportedly employed 3,000 to 5,000, naming no source, and that in March 2023 the company sought Rs 22.7 billion from the state power buyer for a loan repayment.

No independent measure of the effect on farmers was found.

Greenpeace, a campaign group, projected in 2019 that the plant would cause 4,700 premature deaths over its life.

Norfund lists its investment as exited and names no local benefit.

The article notes a writer it quotes advises Bridge and does not name the funder. The result covers learning only, and Bridge's parent later shut most of its Kenyan private schools.

lower-kihansi-dam.whole: KfW, a co-financier, in 2006 rated the 180 MW plant's development effect slightly insufficient (4 on a 6-point scale). It called it "a still successful project" on energy, helping avoid capacity-related grid failures, with output about 12% below target and costs of €212.1 million against €185.0 million. It found "lasting and irreversible damage" to the gorge ecosystem, and flow releases meant to protect it cost about €6.6 million a year in revenue.

It was scaled down in 2015 citing events including Ebola; a West African energy body later gave 400 factory staff and up to 2,000 seasonal workers.

Its funder ADFD claims capacity for over 6,500 GWh a year and doubled national generating capacity, and a trade report, naming no source, says electricity access rose from 15% in 2008 to 30%. A University of Plymouth thesis found electricity and linked projects supported development in the region but social conditions "no better than before the dam"; no measured output from an independent body was found.

three-gorges-eca.whole: The dam was built for flood control, power and shipping. Its operator reported a record 111.8 billion kWh in 2020. A peer-reviewed study in Scientific Reports found the dam and upstream reservoirs together stored 22.7 billion m³ in the July 2016 flood, lowering water levels by 0.8-1.7 m in the Jingjiang reach, while the channel below the dam deepened by an average 1.5 m over 410 km from 2002 to 2014.
three-gorges-eca.searched: Water Power magazine reporting the operator; Yang et al. 2017. Chinese-authored but peer-reviewed.

san-roque-dam-agno.whole: The campaign group FoE Japan says the dam was built mainly for 345 MW of power, with 70,800 to 80,000 hectares of irrigation planned. An operator executive said in May 2024 that about 36,000-40,000 hectares were watered in the last dry season, and the Inquirer reported about 40,000 hectares in 2019. No independent yearly generation figure was found.
san-roque-dam-agno.searched: FoE Japan; Sunday Punch; Inquirer; Bulatlat. JBIC evaluation not found.

kotopanjang-dam.whole: A team of outside academics hired for Japan's aid agency found the 114 MW plant generated 483.7 GWh in 2001 against a target of 697 GWh, later cut to 542, about 20% of electricity supply in Riau and West Sumatra. The report says some resettled families still suffered hardship while others earned from fish farming, and it gives no income figures.
kotopanjang-dam.searched: JICA third-party ex post evaluation, 2004. Funder-commissioned; later output not found.

matarbari-coal-salt-farmers.whole: UNB gives December 2023 for the commissioning of the first unit of the 1,200 MW plant, which has supplied Bangladesh's grid. In April 2024 the plant company's managing director said it had received no payment for that power, a bill of about Tk 700 crore. No generation total or independent assessment of its benefit was found.

kahuzi-biega-batwa.whole: A survey led by the Wildlife Conservation Society, published in 2021, counted 3,815 Grauer's gorillas in the park and adjoining Oku forests, almost 60% of the world's total, and found numbers stable over two decades in the Oku forests and the park's highlands (Mongabay). WCS works in those forests, the count does not isolate what German money did, and no independent check was found.

banskhali-coal-plant.whole: The plant was built to add 1,320 MW to Bangladesh's grid. In February 2024 The Business Standard reported it sending 451 MW, about one-third of capacity, because of grid substation limits. New Age reported in 2025 that it received the highest capacity charge among plants it cited, Tk 7.34 per unit, and no yearly generation total from an independent source was found.

morowali-imip-smelter-deaths.whole: AidData's record, without naming a source, says the financed smelter made 581,000 tons of nickel pig iron and 882,900 tons of steel slab in 2018, with $1.83 billion in sales. A study by the research groups CREA and CELIOS of nickel processing in three provinces, not this park alone, projects about $4 billion in added value in year five against $2.63-3.42 billion a year in health costs and at least 3,800 deaths a year in the next two years.

coca-codo-sinclair.whole: The 1,500 MW plant was designed to supply 8.8 billion kWh a year, 35% of Ecuador's electricity use (AidData's record). The operator reported a record 1,440 MW in November 2023; grid data showed 324 MW, about 20% of capacity, on 10 November 2024, with river flow the lowest for that month since 1964 and no reservoir. The US Energy Information Administration says erosion repairs and complications keep it from full capacity.

las-bambas-2015.whole: The mine started commercial output in July 2016, and MMG expects 280,000-320,000 tonnes of copper a year; its finance chief said in 2023 it had paid over S/ 6.8 billion in taxes and S/ 1.74 billion in royalties. The head of the institute IPE links the mine to Apurímac's halved poverty. The NGO CooperAcción estimates 1,324 of the region's 10,188 direct mining jobs in 2023 went to residents and says Peru's 2006-2017 poverty fall cannot be credited specifically to mining.

sorik-marapi-gas-leak.whole: The geothermal plant's first phase installed 126 MW, and its first unit began supplying the grid in September 2019 (AidData's record). The state utility PLN, which buys the power, said that 45 MW unit cuts production costs by about Rp 6.27 per kWh, with potential savings of about $9.2 million a year. No independent check was found, nor any measure of benefit in Sibanggor Julu.

letpadaung-copper-mine.whole: The mine was designed for 100,000 tons of copper a year and made over 60,000 tons in 2017 (AidData's record, naming no source). A minister told parliament the government earned about $20 million from May 2016 to January 2017. In 2014 Wanbao claimed over 4,000 jobs, while a survey of 57 households in five nearby villages by the NGO Pandita Development Institute reported "no benefits for local residents".
letpadaung-copper-mine.searched: AidData record, DVB reporting ministry figures, RFA reporting the NGO survey. Small sample; no larger independent income study found.

No measured generation or electrification figures were found. Human Rights Watch, cited by AidData, estimated that 16,000 people face displacement and said livelihood restoration had not started by the end of 2019.

No irrigation result or independent output figure was found.

laos-china-railway-land.whole: The line was expected to cut Boten-Vientiane travel from three days to under three hours. The Star, partly quoting the operator's manager, reports nearly 2.6 million passengers and over 4 million tonnes of cargo on the Lao section in 2023, over 3,600 jobs and 800 Lao staff; no independent count was found. Laos borrowed $480 million for its equity share, and a Mahidol University visiting lecturer warned of potential debt distress.

mtwara-gas-pipeline-riots.whole: The pipeline was to carry southern gas to Dar es Salaam for power, industry and other uses, and it opened in October 2015. Tanzania's national auditor reported that by March 2017 the power utility TANESCO was its only customer, taking 46.61 million cubic feet a day against 80 million agreed and a rated capacity of 784 million. The state owner TPDC disclosed default on the on-lent China Eximbank loans as of June 2016, with no payments by June 2021 (AidData's record).

No independent measure of jobs or income was found.

A 2015 UN Human Rights Council report, as quoted by the NATO Association of Canada, calls it the only foreign miner paying royalties and taxes to the treasury. No source found shows what reached Eritreans.

A transparency alliance says Myanmar gets 1% of revenue when nickel is below $15,000 a ton. The record says reports put community spending at K120 million (about $53,000) in a recent year against a $300,000 annual obligation, and a lawmaker confirmed misuse of funds.

President Thein Sein suspended it in September 2011, and it was still suspended at the record's last update in 2018. The advocacy group CDD, backing residents' toll complaints, says 160 meticais a trip means 6,400 a month for a daily return, above the minimum wage, and that those who cannot pay leave cars across the bay.
